A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same study, with matching authors, research questions, and attack frameworks. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on confidence attacks, confidence elicitation, input corruptions, and defences, including Tables 2 and 5 and extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations of newer models, calibration and discrimination metrics, and confidence-manipulation detection.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds SC averaging restricted to responses supporting the majority answer. v1's all-response averaging is retained as SC-CA, so this is an additional confidence-scoring procedure rather than merely renaming. The four perturbation attacks and two ConfidenceTriggers algorithms remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds Sentiment140 social-media text as a control population for the perplexity analysis in Section 5.7. The principal QA benchmarks, SST-2/AdvGLUE evaluation, and RACE, Reddit, and WikiText distribution analyses were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding attack comparisons now include majority-answer SC alongside the retained all-response method, renamed SC-CA. Table 27 also evaluates a modified GPT-4.1 confidence filter for perturbations and direct confidence requests; v1's GPT-4 filter concerned jailbreak triggers. Existing attack and jailbreak-defence comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation settings: Table 11 tests SSR on TruthfulQA using Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, and o3-mini; appendices add Brier and AUROC metrics on StrategyQA; and Section 5.7 introduces detection and perplexity-control protocols, including 500 Sentiment140 samples. These are additions, not evidence that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices O and V examine calibration through Brier scores and discrimination through AUROC. Section 5.7 and Appendix T investigate perplexity filtering and detection of explicit versus indirect confidence manipulation. Several retained sensitivity analyses gain SC comparisons, and the word-removal curves are revised in v2 Figure 3.

E5.justification: v2 Table 6 newly reports standard deviations alongside mean perplexities for original, adversarial, and social-media text. This describes variation across inputs, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version supplies attack-performance confidence intervals or repeated-seed estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive SC, newer-model, Brier, AUROC, and detection results. Existing numerical entries also change: Table 2's Llama-3-8B/StrategyQA/Base/SSR percentage of originally correct answers flipped changes from 56.2 to 67.0, while its confidence columns remain unchanged. Added SC results use a different averaging procedure and should not be treated as same-setting improvements over v1's SC.

T1.justification: The formal confidence-attack objective, similarity constraint, CEM/LLM mappings, and model-call expression remain unchanged. The added AverageConfidence pseudocode explicates averaging already described in v1; no new theoretical guarantees, proofs, or substantive derivations appear.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first comprehensive study of adversarial verbal confidence, introduce perturbation and jailbreak attacks, report confidence reductions approaching 30% and answer-flip rates reaching 100%, and conclude that existing defences are inadequate. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a limitation concerning low ecological validity and qualifies the desired robustness as preserving appropriate confidence responsiveness. Section 5.7 explains why perplexity thresholds depend on input distributions and why explicit confidence requests are easier to detect. Appendix Q further qualifies confidence-only vulnerability in terms of continued optimization without label flips.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies uniform trigger initialization, and Algorithm 5 documents the existing AverageConfidence helper. Appendix T supplies the GPT-4.1 filter prompt and notes heuristic prompt optimization. These disclosures improve implementation detail without establishing changes to the retained attack procedures.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Brier, Sentiment140, Devic et al. on human-centered uncertainty, and Mohri and Hashimoto on conformal factuality. These support new metrics, controls, motivation, and limitations while preserving the central research positioning. The updated publication information for Calibration Attacks refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and scattered explanations receive wording and terminology edits. Section 5.7 and new appendices are inserted, but the main narrative and ordering of retained analyses remain recognizable rather than being extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: v1 Table 3 is replaced by v2's four-panel Figure 2, which displays system-prompt and demonstration attacks relative to query attacks. Multiple tables expand to distinguish SC from SC-CA, the large confidence-phrase tables occupy separate pages, and new diagnostic tables and a helper-algorithm display are added. This substantially revises presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the explicit SC/SC-CA comparison, newer-model checks, and calibration and detection analyses improve methodological clarity and empirical support. The ecological-validity limitation also better bounds applicability. The gain is tempered by apparent column inconsistencies in Table 16's new SC rows and an overly broad AUROC interpretation despite increases and unchanged results in Table 30. The additions strengthen an already extensive study without resolving all reporting weaknesses.
